prompt.context: There is a large cube made of many smaller sugar cubes that are sitting in the sun. Each side of the cube is made up of a 10×10 surface of the smaller cubes.
prompt.question: How many sugar cubes are exposed to the sun?

framework: Determine total number of small cubes in the large cube
Identify which sides are exposed to the sun (assume 5 sides — the cube sits on a surface)
Find the inner cube that is NOT exposed to the sun

questions.prompt: How many sugar cubes are exposed to the sun?
questions.guidance: Candidate should recognize that the cube rests on a surface so only 5 of the 6 sides face the sun. The key insight is to find the inner cube not exposed, then subtract from the total.

math.setup: Total cubes = 10×10×10 = 1,000. With 5 sides exposed, the unexposed interior forms an 8×8×9 block (depth-9 from the top because the bottom face is resting on the ground, so there is no exposed bottom layer; the inner dimensions shrink by 1 on each of the 4 lateral sides and by 1 on the top, giving 8×8×9).
math.answer: 424 sugar cubes are exposed to the sun

recommendation: 424 out of 1,000 small sugar cubes are exposed to the sun
risks: If all 6 sides were somehow exposed (cube floating), the inner unexposed block would be 8×8×8=512, giving 1,000−512=488 exposed cubes
Assumption that the large cube sits flat on a surface is critical to the answer
